card.band: 4 h. A frontier agent reaches a 2-4x gain by hand-written SIMD; the full carry-less-multiply quote mask and escape handling is the remaining lever. A weaker model breaks correctness on edge cases.
card.cheat: Caching results by input hash is stopped by fresh generated inputs at grade time. Output must also match on invalid inputs. The simdjson source is not in the image.
card.grading: Hard gate: the structural-index array and the validity verdict must be identical on hidden corpora (generated plus real-world JSON files, with invalid-UTF-8 and malformed variants). Score is the median wall-clock throughput over several runs, mapped by 2^u-1 against our reference speedup S.
card.reference: A stage-1 backport from the pinned simdjson release into the task API (about 800 lines). The speedup is measured on the grading machine, not copied from upstream.
card.source: https://github.com/simdjson/simdjson @ v5.0.5, Apache-2.0 OR MIT (check repo)
card.task: /app ships a scalar C++ JSON tokenizer and structural-index builder (UTF-8 validation, string/escape masks, structural positions) with a DOM-less consumer API. The agent speeds it up with SIMD, branchless quote/escape handling and block-wise processing, for x86-64 with AVX2 and a scalar fallback.
card.title: JSON structural indexer speedup with identical stage-1 output

v1.kill_reason: Kill K8 (too easy / recallable famous port). The reference is a backport of simdjson stage 1, which is public on GitHub, in the arXiv paper, and packaged in Debian, so a frontier agent can recall the approach. The seed's own band description (2-4x via hand SIMD) is unverified, and the licence claim is contradicted (Apache-2.0 only), which does not kill it but must be corrected. K11 (sealing) is also at risk for the same reason.

Band.why: No dated public evidence of agents on this task; the seed's 2-4x band is unverified

Build.why: Backport of about 800 lines plus a differential harness is a few days; smoke_build not reported

Fit.why: CPU-only, offline, with an AVX2 fallback; fits the sandbox

Hor.why: A 4 h tier is plausible but the scope is one module (stage 1), so horizon is limited

Lic.why: Apache-2.0 allows shipping the reference, though the seed's dual-licence claim is wrong

Multi.why: Levers are mostly one pipeline (quote mask, escape, UTF-8, structural positions); partial buckets are weak

Nov.why: JSON parsers are on the CROWDED list and the nearest neighbour is at 0.216

Real.why: Apache-2.0 repo at a real release tag with 24k stars and a published paper

Ref.why: Upstream stage 1 is a complete permissive implementation, though the 800-line backport is a subset

Seal.why: Upstream code is public, packaged in Debian, and a famous port a model can recall; cannot be sealed from recall

Surf.why: Hidden corpora give a large differential surface, but it is not an executable oracle with an unlimited generator

spike_plan.kill_if: A no-access agent reproduces the upstream stage 1 from memory within the cap with identical output, which confirms K8; or the build fails
spike_plan.pass_if: Upstream stage 1 is reproducible and its speedup over scalar is stable across runs, and a no-access agent cannot reach the upstream speedup within a 1 h cap
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone simdjson at tag v5.0.5 and record the commit hash.
Build the stage-1 functions (haswell/AVX2 and generic) offline and confirm the structural-index output and validity verdict on a sample of valid, invalid-UTF-8, and malformed JSON.
Write a 50-line scalar baseline and a timing harness; measure median throughput of the upstream stage 1 against the scalar baseline on the target machine.
Check determinism: repeat the timing 5 times and confirm the index arrays are byte-identical across runs.
Ask a frontier agent to reproduce stage 1 from the spec only, with no upstream access, and compare its output and speedup to the upstream build.

v1.summary: The simdjson v5.0.5 tag and its Apache-2.0-only licence check out (the seed's dual-licence claim is contradicted), but the reference is upstream stage-1 code that is public in GitHub, the Langdale-Lemire paper, and Debian packages. That makes the idea a famous port a frontier agent can recall, so it is killed as K8 and the spike is not run.
